items.title: Stream a synthetic HTTP log summary
items.goal: Summarize a single-pass iterable of synthetic log lines without loading the input into memory.
acceptance: Define the complete synthetic format as four ASCII fields separated by exactly one ASCII space: timestamp method path status. Match the whole line against [0-9]+ [A-Z]+ /[A-Za-z0-9/_-]* [1-5][0-9]{2}. This is not an Apache/nginx log parser.

Each input string may have one terminal LF or CRLF, removed before matching; an unterminated final line is valid. Blank lines, bare CR, extra spaces/fields, invalid methods/paths and out-of-range statuses are malformed: skip them and increment malformed_lines, without aborting the stream.

Return valid_lines, malformed_lines and sparse status_counts keyed by integer HTTP status. Every valid line increments exactly one status count; empty input returns zero counters and an empty mapping. Only these summary counters are retained.

Run offline stdlib unittest cases for normal mixed statuses, empty input, statuses 100/599, timestamp 0, LF/CRLF/no final newline, malformed cases and a single-pass generator. Explain linear time in input characters and memory proportional to distinct statuses, excluding the current line.

items.title: Expose the log summary as a small CLI
items.goal: Wrap the specified synthetic-log summary in a predictable argparse interface.
acceptance: Accept an explicit UTF-8 input path or '-' for stdin; document arguments and the inherited EP-001 format and malformed-line policy.

Write deterministic JSON to stdout with status-count keys represented as JSON strings; diagnostics go to stderr. Missing/unreadable files, decoding errors and usage errors are nonzero exits; counted malformed lines alone are not fatal.

Keep parsing/summary logic separate from argument handling. If prerequisite code is unavailable or unapproved, include a self-contained implementation in this review bundle rather than applying an earlier proposal.
Run offline unittest cases for file/stdin equivalence, empty input, malformed lines, help/usage and read/decode errors; include a real local CLI subprocess smoke test using sys.executable.

items.title: Count and rank the top K synthetic paths
items.goal: Compare a heap-based top-K selection with a straightforward reference implementation.
acceptance: Consume an iterable of synthetic path strings and a nonnegative integer K; reject negative, boolean or non-integer K. Return at most K (path, count) pairs sorted by descending count, then ascending path for ties.
Define empty input, K=0, K greater than distinct-path count and repeated paths. Keep counting memory proportional to distinct paths; do not claim total O(K) memory for exact counts.
Implement heap-based selection and compare its results with a small full-sort reference over deterministic generated fixtures; explain counting and selection time/space separately.
Run offline unittest normal, tie, empty, K-boundary, invalid-K and generator cases. No online judge, network or copied challenge statement is required.

items.title: Track recent server errors in a sliding window
items.goal: Use a deque to calculate a recent error count over an ordered synthetic event stream.
acceptance: Accept nondecreasing integer timestamps and statuses 100..599 with a positive integer window W. For each current event at t, count 5xx events already seen in the prefix with timestamps in (t-W, t], including the current event if it is 5xx.
Specify duplicate timestamps and exact left-edge eviction; reject decreasing timestamps, invalid statuses and invalid W rather than silently sorting or changing the input.
Use a deque and explain amortized linear processing and memory proportional to retained active error events, not a universal constant bound.
Run offline unittest cases for normal windows, empty input, duplicates, no errors, left-edge equality, large timestamp gaps and invalid input; compare against a small prefix-scan reference.

items.title: Calculate a synthetic request-based availability SLI
items.goal: Make the event denominator and availability definition explicit before computing a ratio.
acceptance: Take validated counts for HTTP statuses 100..599. Eligible requests are all valid log records; good=100..499 and bad=500..599. Malformed records are excluded and reported separately, not converted to success.

Return eligible/good/bad counts and an exact fractions.Fraction SLI good/eligible, or None when eligible=0. Explain that treating 4xx as good is a deliberate exercise policy, not a universal SRE definition.
Reject negative, boolean or non-integer counts and invalid status keys. Do not claim these synthetic fixtures measure an actual service's availability.
Run offline unittest cases for mixed, all-good, all-bad, 4xx-only, zero eligible, malformed-only and invalid counts; verify exact ratios before presentation rounding.

items.title: Calculate a request-based error budget
items.goal: Derive allowed failures and signed remaining budget from an explicit objective and synthetic counts.
acceptance: Accept eligible/bad nonnegative integer counts with bad<=eligible and an exact Fraction objective in (0,1]. Compute allowed=eligible*(1-objective), remaining=allowed-bad and consumed=bad/allowed when allowed>0, otherwise None.
Keep fractional allowed failures exact and remaining signed: do not silently round the budget or clamp overspend to zero. Explain the zero-budget/zero-traffic cases explicitly.
Describe this as a single synthetic request-count calculation, not production SLO compliance, a time-based budget or a multi-window burn-rate alert.
Run offline unittest cases for under/exact/over budget, objective=1, zero traffic, invalid objectives and inconsistent counts; use exact Fraction assertions.

items.title: Run a local diagnostic child with a timeout
items.goal: Handle success, nonzero exit and timeout as distinct observable subprocess outcomes.
acceptance: Pass an argv sequence with shell=False and an explicit positive timeout; return a documented structured outcome with exit code, stdout/stderr and timeout indication. Do not interpret a failed child as success.
Use only synthetic local child programs launched with sys.executable in fixtures; no network, real service control, shell pipelines or credential-bearing environment is needed.
Handle timeout and process cleanup for the tested direct child. Document that this is neither an OS security sandbox nor proof of controlling arbitrary descendant processes.
Run actual offline unittest subprocess cases for success, stderr/nonzero exit, timeout and invalid timeout. Record observed results; do not substitute mocked execution for the entire test suite.

items.title: Implement bounded retry with an injectable clock
items.goal: Test retry scheduling deterministically without network access or real sleeps.
acceptance: Inject the operation, monotonic clock and sleep function; validate positive max_attempts and documented nonnegative initial delay/capped exponential backoff settings.
Retry only explicitly declared transient exceptions. Return immediately on success, propagate permanent exceptions unchanged, and re-raise the final transient exception on exhaustion.

A configured monotonic deadline prevents starting an attempt at or after that instant and prevents sleeping beyond it. Explain that a scheduling deadline cannot interrupt an already running operation; operation timeouts are separate.

Run offline unittest cases using a fake clock for immediate/eventual success, attempts exhausted, permanent error, capped delays, exact deadline boundary and invalid configuration. No real sleeps or external endpoints in these tests.

items.title: Validate an offline AI-style JSON response
items.goal: Treat AI-shaped output as untrusted data and enforce a small explicit contract without model calls.
acceptance: Accept JSON text with exactly two root fields: summary is a nonblank string; labels is a list of unique strings drawn from info, warning, error. Reject extra/missing fields and wrong types.
Use stdlib json with explicit rejection of duplicate object keys and nonstandard NaN/Infinity values. Define malformed JSON errors and return a stable validation result rather than executing content.
Fixtures are synthetic AI-style outputs, not responses from an actual model. Strings remain inert data; validation is not a claim of general prompt-injection protection.
Run offline unittest normal/empty-label cases, wrong roots/types, blank summaries, duplicate/unknown labels, duplicate keys, nonstandard numbers and invalid JSON.

items.title: Evaluate a versioned fixture set
items.goal: Measure a validator against fixed synthetic expectations with transparent denominators.
acceptance: Define a small versioned fixture format with unique case IDs, raw response text and expected validity; valid cases additionally declare the expected label set. Reject malformed fixture definitions and duplicate IDs.

Report total cases, exact matches and per-case mismatches. A match requires expected validity and, for valid cases, the expected labels. Exact-match ratio is None for an empty set, not a perfect score.

Show fixture revision and the real locally calculated numerator/denominator. Label the result as synthetic fixture evaluation only: no real-model benchmark, generalization, quality or job-experience claims.
Run offline unittest cases for all/mixed/no matches, empty fixtures, duplicate IDs and malformed fixtures; test the evaluator with a deliberately wrong validator as well as a correct one.

items.title: Validate allowlisted tool requests without execution
items.goal: Separate a proposed tool call's data contract from permission to run anything.
acceptance: Validate a JSON object with exactly tool and arguments: tool must be summarize_log; arguments must contain exactly sample_id, a string from a documented fixed synthetic-fixture allowlist.
Reject unknown tools/keys, duplicate object keys, wrong types and non-allowlisted IDs. Paths, URLs and command text are never interpreted as sample IDs or permission.
Return only a validated data object or explicit errors. Do not dispatch tools, execute shell commands, evaluate code or access arbitrary files; explain that schema validity is not authorization.
Run offline unittest cases for valid fixtures, unknown tools/IDs, path-like IDs, extra/missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys and malformed JSON.

items.title: Parse and validate a small report configuration
items.goal: Use an explicit configuration contract rather than silent environment-dependent defaults.
acceptance: Parse INI text with stdlib configparser and interpolation disabled. Require exactly [report] with top_k, window_seconds and target; reject DEFAULT entries, duplicate definitions, unknown sections/keys and missing fields.
Require top_k and window_seconds to be positive decimal integers and target to be a finite decimal objective in (0,1], converted exactly to Fraction. Document accepted lexical forms and errors.
Do not expand environment variables, load secrets or install parser/schema packages. Supply only a sanitized synthetic configuration example.
Run offline unittest cases for valid/boundary objectives, zero/negative values, nonfinite target, duplicate/unknown/missing fields and interpolation-like literal input.

items.title: Render a deterministic synthetic reliability report
items.goal: Keep presentation stable and separate from SLI/error-budget calculations.
acceptance: Document a compact versioned JSON report contract containing valid/malformed and good/bad counts, SLI, objective, allowed/remaining budget, consumed ratio, ranked top_paths, window_seconds and final-prefix error-window count (null when there are no valid events); keep the renderer pure and free of file/network access.
Represent exact Fraction values using documented numerator/denominator objects and unavailable ratios as JSON null; do not round, clamp negative remaining budget or turn missing data into success.
Produce deterministic UTF-8-compatible JSON text with stable key order and one final newline. Mark the report as synthetic exercise data, not production monitoring.
Run offline unittest cases against exact expected output for normal, empty and overspent cases; verify serialization stability and that rendering does not mutate its input.

items.title: Integrate a small offline reliability report CLI
items.goal: Compose a bounded synthetic-log-to-report path with explicit configuration and real end-to-end tests.
acceptance: Read an explicit synthetic-log file and validated configuration; compose summary, top-K paths, the final event's error-window count, SLI and budget into the deterministic EP-013 report. Use each configuration field and require nondecreasing valid-event timestamps, explicitly rejecting decreasing input rather than sorting silently.
Make required modules available in this new bundle if previous proposals are pending/rejected/absent; do not apply unapproved prerequisites or assume publication/learning from depends_on.

Document run/test commands, expected fixture output, stderr and nonzero exits for configuration/read/decode failures, and the inherited malformed-line policy. No network, model API, Docker or cloud is required.

Run actual offline unittest end-to-end CLI subprocess cases with sys.executable for normal, empty, malformed-only and over-budget fixtures plus bad configuration, missing files and decreasing timestamps; include a top-K tie and an exact window boundary. Record actual counts/output and limitations; do not claim a deployed monitoring service.
